task.description: Validate DDL-02, ORD-01, ORD-02, ORD-04 (all MUST) are ready for release. All prior gates PASSED, including one resolved rework cycle at Step 1b (DDL-02 AC5 byte-offset gap) and a genuine-concurrency-test upgrade at Step 3 that also surfaced ISS-0669/GH-709 (Pool.acquire() thread-contention bug, correctly forwarded not fixed inline -- TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already independently confirmed production code does not hit this bug). Read every AC in all 4 requirement bodies and cross-check real test evidence. Confirm migration idempotency (zig build migrate twice, clean no-op). Assess whether ISS-0669 forwarding was genuinely correct (final sign-off) or whether it should actually block this release.
acceptance_criteria: All MUST requirement ACs have passing integration test evidence
No deferred/skipped coverage on any MUST requirement AC
ISS-0669 forwarding reassessed as correct (not release-blocking) with independent reasoning

result.summary: Release APPROVED for Stage 16 batch WF02-batch-2-20260811 (DDL-02, ORD-01, ORD-02, ORD-04, all MUST). Read every AC in all 4 requirement bodies from docs/requirements.yaml and cross-checked against actual test source: ddl_validate.zig (28 tests, 7 DDL-02-specific covering AC1-AC5 plus tiebreak/conservative), ordering/observability.zig (4 unit tests), ord01/ord04 schema integration tests (3+4), and ordering_consumer_test.zig (10 tests including the genuine multi-OS-thread concurrency tests TC-ORD-01-AC1-concurrent and TC-ORD-04-AC1-concurrent). Independently re-ran every layer myself, all exit 0 matching the test report. Migration idempotency confirmed: zig build migrate run twice with BPM_DB_URL/BPM_TEST_DB_URL set explicitly, both runs clean no-op ("No new migrations to apply", exit 0). zig build bench run for completeness, all 5 NFR checks pass. ISS-0669/GH-709 REASSESSED independently, not just trusted from TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR: the Pool.acquire() thread-contention bug is real and would genuinely block a FUTURE production deployment that wires consumer_count (8) concurrent consumer loops as raw std.Thread.spawn threads sharing one Pool -- that is exactly ISS-0669's repro scenario and exactly what ORD-04's requirement implies for production. However it does NOT block THIS batch: verified by reading src/ordering/consumer.zig in full (no Thread.spawn anywhere in src/ordering/*.zig; runOneCycle/pollLoopStep each acquire one connection synchronously per call) and by grepping src/main.zig, src/scheduler/scheduler.zig, src/effects/worker.zig for pollLoopStep/runOneCycle/ordering_consumer/consumer_count -- zero matches. This batch's consumer loop is not wired into any production executable yet; the design doc (src/design/ord-01-02-04-correlated-effect-reentry.md Open Question 1) explicitly defers the multi-consumer threading/wiring mechanism to a future batch as a non-blocking wiring choice. This batch therefore introduces zero new production callers of the broken code path. Recommendation carried forward in the release decision file: whichever future batch wires consumer_count concurrent loops into production must treat ISS-0669/GH-709 as a hard pre-requisite gate before choosing a raw-thread deployment.
